subject: Private telemetry handoff — SIEM ingestion and tracehook alignment
messages:
From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
To: Jules Bryant <jules@acmecorp.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 21 Nov 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Private telemetry handoff — SIEM ingestion and tracehook alignment

Hi Jules,

Thanks for agreeing to the telemetry handoff call last week. As discussed, this thread captures the concrete items we need to validate for AcmeCorp's private deployment (VPC peering) so Redwood can start streaming logs/metrics and OTLP traces into your SIEM in a compliant way. Key checkpoints:

- Ingest endpoints: what host(s)/port(s) you'll expose on the peered side (Splunk HEC, or a proxy).
- Auth: token vs mutual TLS (we prefer mTLS for private peering) and cert exchange process.
- Network: egress IPs/redwood NATs to allow in your firewall, plus expected packet sizes and connection cadence.
- Payloads: field catalogue and any PII-scrubbing we must apply pre-transmit.
- Tracing: OTLP endpoint, recommended sampling for production vs canary, and the tracehook header conventions so we can correlate spans with request ids.
- Canary: a short test window, expected ingest volume, and rollback/fallback plan.

I've attached a compact telemetry_field_map_v1.xlsx (field -> index mapping) and tracehook-endpoint-spec.md (proposed OTLP headers and TLS requirements). Can you confirm the HEC/proxy host you'll provide and whether your SIEM supports client certs, or if you require a bearer token? Also, please share the network contact who will accept Redwood's egress IPs.

Proposed next step: 2-hour canary window in UTC between Nov 29 01:00-03:00 (low-traffic). If that works we'll provide a short runbook and a proof-of-transfer checklist.

Thanks —
Markus
Markus Klein
Head of Infrastructure Partnerships
Redwood Inference

Markus —

Thanks for the summary. We can definitely take a peered HEC endpoint. A few clarifications from our side:

- Host: we will expose hec-private.acme.splunk.internal on the peered VPC (TLS required). Final FQDN will be provided once network peering is live.
- Auth: Splunk supports both token and mTLS. Security prefers mTLS for this lane; token-only is acceptable for short-lived test flows.
- Network contact: looping in Tim Shao (timothy.shao@acmecorp.com) who handles peering and firewall rules.
- Field mapping: we'll review your spreadsheet and get back with required index names or automatic mapping options.
- Trace ingestion: we support OTLP over TLS; please include resource attributes for service.name and deployment.environment in each span.

We have an internal compliance checklist for customer telemetry that includes retention caps and masking rules. I'll attach the checklist after Tim confirms the network details.

On the canary window — Nov 29 01:00-03:00 UTC sounds fine tentatively; Tim will confirm once we have peering scheduled.

Hi Jules / Tim (cc),

Adding the operational details we've committed to from Redwood's side so the network and security teams have concrete values to work against:

1) Ingest endpoints
  - Splunk HEC (private): hec-private.us-west-2.acme.splunk.internal:8088 (TLS). We'll also support an in-VPC HTTP proxy if required.
  - Trace OTLP: otlp-ingest.redwood.internal:4317 (mTLS + ALPN http/2).

2) Auth & certs
  - Preferred: mutual TLS with certs issued by Redwood's CA for the dedicated peering account.
  - Fallback for canary: short-lived bearer token with rotation (48h).
  - Cert exchange: we'll generate a CSR and provide public certs via our secure doc share; please confirm preferred SFTP or signed S3 presigned URL.

3) Network & firewall
  - Redwood egress NAT IPs for the peering block: [52.34.170.12, 52.34.170.13, 52.34.170.14] (these are static for the dedicated pool).
  - Ports: 8088 (HEC), 4317 (OTLP), 443 for proxy.
  - Keep-alive: we use persistent HTTP/1.1/2 connections with occasional reconnects; average burst ~200 msg/s during canary, expect 90th percentile payload ~1.2KB.

4) Payload & privacy
  - We'll apply the field mapping in telemetry_field_map_v1.xlsx pre-ingest. Any fields flagged as PII will be redacted by default; please send any additional required scrubbing rules.
  - We also support sample-level hashing of user IDs as an alternative for joins.

5) Tracing specifics
  - Headers: x-redwood-traceid, x-redwood-spanid, x-redwood-sampled (true/false).
  - Resource attrs required: service.name, deployment.environment, region.
  - Sampling: we propose 5% production sampling initially and 100% for the canary window for full verification.

6) Canary & rollback
  - Proposed canary: Nov 29 01:00-03:00 UTC (100% tracing, capped ingest volume 250 events/s).
  - Fallback: immediate cutoff and switch to token-based buffered delivery if anything looks abnormal.

7) Runbook & checklist
  - Runbook: https://drive.google.com/open?id=runbook-acmecorp-peering (access shared to acme team).
  - Proof-of-transfer checklist: we'll request a signed confirmation after the canary that includes sample event IDs, timestamp ranges, and hash proofs.

Action items we need from Acme:
- Confirm host FQDN once peering is provisioned.
- Confirm mTLS vs token preference and the method for cert exchange.
- Open firewall rules for the three NAT IPs and ports above.
- Identify a point-of-contact for the canary window and provide a Slack/IRC channel for real-time ops.
